column1: # local-watch-attribution.tsv — FDY-91.
# 41 REAL headlines, captured read-only from public.artifacts on
# ycadmmngkdhvpcsrcuaq, 2026-10-07/08. Every row is a local-watch artifact
# (source_registry.source_key like 'gsearch:loc-%') whose raw_content matches
# 'data ?cent' and whose published_at >= 2026-07-01, with Google's
# " - <publisher>" suffix stripped by headline-pure.ts extractHeadline().
# The verdict columns are NOT hand-written. They are the output of
# scripts/boundstone-local-push-dryrun.sql, which re-implements the same three
# attribution rules in SQL so the whole 6,157-row corpus can be measured at
# once. test/boundstone-local-push.test.mjs runs attribution-pure.ts over these
# rows and asserts it agrees with the SQL, row for row. That is what keeps the
# dry-run totals in the PR body honest: if the TypeScript and the SQL ever
# disagree, this file is the tripwire.
# Rows are grouped by what they are here to prove:
#   1-3    the three cases the brief names by hand
#   4-7    s3_abbr_agrees — a USPS code agreeing with a jurisdiction
#   8-15   s2_unique_jurisdiction — a county unique to one state nationally
#   16-25  s1_state_name — an unambiguous full state name
#   26-31  DECLINED ambiguous_jurisdiction — the county exists in >1 state
#   32-34  DECLINED ambiguous_state_named — two states named at once
#   35-41  DECLINED no_honest_state — nothing in the headline establishes one
# ⚠️ ROW 1 IS THE WHOLE POINT. "Michigan City Council to consider data center
# moratorium" is Michigan City, INDIANA. It DECLINES, because the compound-place
# guard drops the bare "Michigan" and nothing else in the headline proves
# Indiana. A naive full-name scan files it under MI, on a public state page.
# ⚠️ ROW 3. The brief expected "Sedgwick County KS". Production disagrees and
# production wins: Sedgwick County exists in BOTH Kansas and Colorado, so the
# headline alone does not establish the state and the row is declined. A smaller
# true number beats a larger false one.
# ⚠️ ROW 4 is deliberately ugly. It is a real artifact whose first RSS line is a
# whole paragraph, not a headline. It is kept verbatim, truncation and all,
# because the corpus contains rows like it and a fixture of only tidy headlines
# would not prove the code survives the real ones.
# headline<TAB>state_abbr<TAB>jurisdiction_name<TAB>state_rule<TAB>reason
# Empty means NULL in all four verdict columns.
